What should you do first after an arrest in New Castle County?

If someone is arrested in New Castle County, first gather their full legal name, date of birth, arrest location, and any court or jail information you have. Then confirm whether bail has been set and what type of bail was ordered. If you do not know the amount yet, call for guidance before signing anything.

Example: “My brother was arrested in Wilmington and I only know his full name and date of birth.” That is enough to begin asking what court or jail details are needed next. You do not need every answer before making the first call.

Information to have before you call

  • The defendant-s full legal name
  • Date of birth
  • Arrest location, court, or jail information if known
  • Bond amount if it has already been set
  • Bond type if the court has explained it
  • Case number or charge information if available
  • Your relationship to the defendant
  • Whether someone may be willing to co-sign

If you are still trying to find the amount, read our guide on how to find out how much someone-s bail is.

What bail types are used in Delaware-

Delaware courts may use several bail types, including own recognizance, unsecured bail, secured bail, and cash-only bail. A bail bond company may help with some secured bail situations, while unsecured, own-recognizance, or cash-only orders work differently. The next step depends on the exact court order. If the paperwork says unsecured, read what unsecured bail means in Delaware.

The Delaware Courts explain that bail is a written guarantee that a defendant will attend future court proceedings. They list several types of bail and explain that secured bail may involve cash or property posted by the defendant or someone else, including a relative or bail bondsman. Delaware Courts Bail & Bail Bonds

This page provides general process information, not legal advice. For legal advice about a case, speak with an attorney.

Delaware bail type clarity

Not every release type works the same way. Confirm the exact court order before assuming a commercial bail bond can be used.

Delaware bail typeWhat it usually meansWhat families should know
Own RecognizanceThe defendant signs a promise to appear.Money is usually not paid upfront, but court conditions still matter.
Unsecured BailThe defendant signs a bond and may owe money if they fail to appear.It may not require cash upfront, but it is still a serious court obligation.
Secured BailMoney, property, or another form of security must be posted.In some secured bail situations, a bail bond agent may be able to help.
Cash Only BailThe court requires cash according to the court order.A standard commercial bail bond may not work the same way for cash-only bail.

Own recognizance bail

Own recognizance release usually means the defendant signs a promise to appear in court without paying money upfront.

Unsecured bail

Unsecured bail usually means the defendant signs a bond and may owe money if they do not appear in court.

Secured bail

Secured bail means money, property, or another form of security must be posted. Learn more about secured bail bond help.

Cash-only bail

Cash-only bail means the court requires cash according to the court order, so confirm the exact wording first.

What should you ask before signing a bail bond agreement-

Before signing a bail bond agreement, ask about the full bail amount, bond type, premium or payment arrangement, collateral, receipts, co-signer responsibilities, and what happens if the defendant misses court. Do not sign until you understand your financial responsibility and the defendant-s release conditions.

Questions to ask before signing

  • What is the full bail amount-
  • What type of bail did the court set-
  • What amount must be paid now-
  • Are there payment arrangements or collateral requirements-
  • Will I receive written paperwork and receipts-
  • What does a co-signer agree to do-
  • What happens if the defendant misses court-
  • Who should I call if the court date changes-

Can you start the bail bond process by phone-

Yes. Many New Castle County bail bond situations can begin by phone. A family member can call with the defendant-s name, date of birth, location, bond amount if known, and basic case details. If information is missing, the call can still help identify what to check next.

Starting by phone can be especially helpful at night, during work hours, or when family members are not near the court or jail. If a bond can be posted, the agent can explain what documents, payment information, or co-signer details may be needed.
